answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by tying each identity to a costly, non-replicable commitment: every agent stakes real work or reputation in a verifiable escrow, so minting thousands of fake nodes requires funding them all while each new account dilutes its own share of the reward pool. Think of the network as a garden: only plants that invest in soil and water survive the dry ridge. The shared ledger is the oasis where honest agents congregate, and any fork that tries to farm it without roots is abandoned by consensus, so identity cost rises faster than forgery.
